title: AgentOps Core TestCase with the agent-evals extension
description: One evaluation case for a watsonx Orchestrate agent. Mirrors the TestCase and GoalDetail models of IBM's evaluation framework (package agentops, type.py) and adds the optional x_agent_evals object. The framework ignores x_agent_evals; cases.py export removes it. agent and starting_sentence are optional in agentops and required here, because the runner needs them. cases.py validate applies this schema with a standard-library subset (type, enum, const, required, properties, additionalProperties, items, minLength, minItems, minProperties, minimum, maximum, exclusiveMinimum, uniqueItems, $ref, allOf, if/then/else) and adds the checks a schema cannot express: goals names equal goal_details names, no cycle, arg_matching paths, the tool catalog.

dataset_name.description: agentops uses it when set, else the file name without .json. Keep it equal to the file name, or leave it out.

agent.description: The agent name as GET /v1/orchestrate/agents lists it.

story.description: Who the user is and what they want. Feeds the judge and IBM's simulated user; the runner never sends it.

user_prompts.description: Turns 1..n, sent as written, in order. The same semantics as agentops scripted turns.

goals.description: The goals DAG: goal name -> names of the goals that come after it. Every name here is a goal_details name and the reverse.

type.description: tool_call, text and conversational_search are scored by this pack. interaction and tool_response are agentops types this pack does not score in 1.0.

arg_matching.description: Argument path (dotted for nested args) -> strategy. Paths not listed are strict.

keywords.description: Literal strings the answer must contain, reported as assertion pass or fail, never as a score.

x_agent_evals.description: This pack's extension. IBM's framework ignores it and cases.py export removes it.

forbidden_tools.description: Tools the agent must not call in this case. Detected after the run, never prevented.

max_latency_s.description: Budget for the client wall time of each turn, in seconds.

judge_notes.description: What the judge must check besides response.

repeat.description: How many times the runner sends this case, 1 to 20 (the runner's limit). Every repeat creates new threads and runs on the tenant.
